name: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd
title: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd - 541729 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset manager with QAAUM up 20% to INR9.3tn and FY26 PAT up 16% to INR28.6bn; flows strong but TER/BER regulation trims distributor economics, with gross impact 3-4 bps on existing book.

triggers.quote: equity was around 56 basis points, debt 28 and liquid 13. And blended for the year was 45.

summary.headline: HDFC AMC FY26 profit after tax rose 16% to INR28.6 billion; QAAUM grew 20% to INR9.3 trillion and dividend of INR54 per share was recommended.
summary.overview: HDFC AMC closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR41.2 billion (up 18% YoY), operating profit of INR32.1 billion (up 18%, 35 bps of AUM) and PAT of INR28.6 billion (up 16%). QAAUM reached INR9.3 trillion (up 20%), with equity-oriented AUM at INR6 trillion and unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million. Management highlighted record March 2026 SIP flows of INR321 billion industry-wide and said investor behaviour during the market correction was disciplined. The major open issue is the SEBI base expense ratio (BER) change effective April 1, 2026, which management expects to offset through commission changes with no material P&L impact.

segments.name: Equity-oriented funds
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion. Actively managed equity yield was about 60-61 bps, versus 56 bps including index funds.

segments.name: Debt and liquid funds
segments.commentary: Debt yield was 28 bps and liquid 13 bps in Q4. Management said the balance sheet debt book is run with modest duration and largely passive management.

segments.name: Alternatives, PMS and international
segments.commentary: Alternatives margins are marginally above equity margins, and discretionary PMS is in line with equity margins. Non-discretionary EPFO/SPFO mandates earn thinner net economics. GIFT City has five live funds, all wholly owned.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gross impact of the base expense ratio change on existing book at about 3-4 bps, to be largely offset by commission restructuring and cost management, so targeted P&L impact is not material.
The 5 bps trail previously paid in lieu of exit load has been removed, and GST on management fees now sits outside the expense ratio, requiring margin adjustments.

No formal cost guidance is given. Employee cost ex-ESOP grew about 12.5% YoY, with five-year CAGRs of about 13% for employee cost and 13.5% for non-employee cost; costs are expected to grow broadly in line with business.
Management said flow market share is above book market share, and the company will launch SIF products only after careful design, not as a race.
Management said the SEBI-classified category presence is complete and new launches will be selective, with focus on sharpening existing funds.
capex_capacity: Physical branch network significantly expanded over the last couple of years, with further expansion under evaluation.
Investment in AI, cloud technology, cybersecurity and talent for PMS, international and alternatives; management called these foundational investments.
Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.
Seven new schemes launched in FY26, and first close of a private credit fund with IFC as partner and anchor investor announced.
Two EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates won. SPFO is already being managed, and the EPFO agreement is being signed.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 net inflows INR7.4 trillion, with equity-oriented funds about INR4.9 trillion; March 2026 SIP collections INR321 billion (up 24% YoY, 97 million contributing accounts). Industry market share is around 12.8-13% for the last eight to nine quarters.
HDFC AMC: direct plans about 31% of equity AUM; 97% of transactions digital; total accounts above 30 million; unique investors 16.7 million, up 3.5 million, versus industry addition of 7.2 million.
Unique investor penetration rose from 17.6% (March 2023) to 27% (March 2026). Folios rose from 2.3 crore to 3 crore, and SIP and STP flows were INR48.8 billion in March 2026 (up 33% YoY).

Management said flow share is higher than book share across channels, including fintech and HDFC Securities. HDFC Bank share of the distribution pie is declining, which management attributed to broad-based growth across other channels.
Competitive pressure: management stated SBI is almost closed-architecture, and some banks are more guided in retail distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new TER/BER regulation and how will distribution commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross impact on the existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset through commission optimisation and cost management, so no material P&L impact is targeted. New commission structures already reflect removal of the 5 bps exit-load trail, and the company will share more detail over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a third-party calculation show Q4 flow market share below Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the calculation missed IDCW (dividend) payouts in Q4 that were recorded as redemptions; the company does not accept the computed figure. Management said overall flow share remains above book share.

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds remain in the top two quartiles across most categories and that many are rated 4 or 5 stars by Value Research. It pointed to long-term alpha track records, with 12-13 funds having 15-year-plus records.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

risks_watch: SEBI base expense ratio change from April 1, 2026: margin effect depends on commission restructuring, and management said the impact is not yet quantified precisely.
Sustainability of flows if markets stay weak for longer; management cautioned that investor behaviour has not been tested over an extended downturn.
HDFC Bank channel share is declining, and management said the bank remains open architecture, with event-driven flow variability.
Rising costs from talent, technology and AI investments versus margin targets, with no formal cost guidance.
Alternatives and PMS economics are thinner for non-discretionary government mandates (EPFO/SPFO), and SIF launch timing is undefined.
Mark-to-market exposure on the SEBI skin-in-the-game equity holdings on the balance sheet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on flows, investor maturity and long-term growth, but defensive on market share, the HDFC Bank channel and performance ranking. Management was cautious and non-committal on cost guidance, SIF timing and the quantified TER impact, saying it is still early.
key_quotes: And that clearly shows a very mature behaviour of investors.
So overall, the targeted impact on our P&L should not be material.
So overall flows are higher than the book share, that much I can tell you.
Real question is, how do we participate in a way that is consistent with our philosophy?

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross BER change from April 1, 2026 is about 3-4 bps on the existing book, management targets offset via commission restructuring so no material P&L impact, yet FY26 operating margin was 35 bps of AUM and blended yield 45 bps with cost growth ~12.5% YoY ex-ESOP.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network expanded significantly over last couple of years with further expansion under evaluation, but no number, size or date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: QAAUM up 20% to INR9.3 trillion in FY26, unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million, and March 2026 SIP flows up 24% YoY to INR321 billion industry-wide, with management saying flow share is above book share.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance is given and management is non-committal on cost and TER impact, so there is no basis for an upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: BER change and loss of 5 bps exit-load trail carry a 3-4 bps gross impact on existing book, and the quantified impact is not yet known; flows could weaken if markets stay weak longer.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Seven new schemes launched in FY26 and SIF regulatory approvals secured, but management calls SIF strategic rather than immediate and will stay selective, with no date given.

rows.label: SEBI BER/TER change from April 1, 2026
rows.why: Gross impact on existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset via commission restructuring, and management says the quantified P&L effect is not yet precise.

rows.label: Private credit fund first close with IFC as anchor
rows.why: First close already announced with IFC as partner and anchor investor, opening the alternatives business.

rows.label: EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates
rows.why: Two mandates won, SPFO already being managed and EPFO agreement being signed, though these earn thinner net economics.

tone.note: Management was confident on flows, investor maturity and long-term growth but defensive on market share, HDFC Bank channel share and one-year performance ranking, and cautious on cost guidance, SIF timing and the quantified TER impact; analysts pushed on flow share and scheme rankings.
